title: Beatrix and the Interior
premise: Cyrus Nakamura, a piano tuner who reads a house's history through its radiators and pipes, attends the funeral of the woman whose piano he tuned for twenty years — and is addressed by a stranger using a family name no one has spoken aloud since 1974. The stranger, Ada, carries an untranslated sentence written by the dead woman's brother, a dissident who vanished before Cyrus was born, and claims only someone who can 'hear' the house can finish translating it. As Cyrus deciphers the sentence hidden in the house's very acoustics, they uncover that the family's respectability was built on a betrayal the law never touched, forcing them to choose between exposing it and protecting the living relatives who finally made them feel they belonged. In the end, Cyrus speaks the sentence aloud at the house's last gathering, trading their hard-won place in the family for the justice the sentence demands.
about_author: Jonah Okonkwo is the pen name of a former building superintendent who spent fifteen years listening to the pipes of pre-war apartment houses. They write about the secret histories rooms keep, and live above a laundromat whose boiler they refuse to have replaced.

chapters.title: The Tuner's Ear
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the funeral of Marguerite Voss, whose piano he tuned for two decades, Cyrus performs his perfected smile and prepares to leave unnoticed — until a stranger named Ada greets him by a name nobody uses: the family's original surname, retired in 1974. The emotional beat is the crack in Cyrus's armor: belonging offered by a total stranger at the moment of greatest grief.

chapters.title: What the Radiators Remember
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with Ada present. Ada reveals an unfinished sentence in the hand of Marguerite's vanished brother, insisting its final words are encoded in the house itself. Cyrus, skeptical but unable to resist, begins mapping the building's sounds — discovering a rhythm in the radiators that matches the sentence's cadence. Rising tension: the house confirms Ada's claim, and Cyrus realizes the family name change hid something deliberate.

chapters.title: The Untranslatable Sentence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Cyrus and Marguerite's daughter Lise. The translation completes: the brother's sentence names who denounced him to the authorities — Marguerite herself, then a young woman securing the family's future. Lise, reading over Cyrus's shoulder, threatens to destroy the page; Cyrus must choose between the family that finally claimed them and the truth. Climax: Cyrus refuses to stay silent, and Lise turns them out of the house mid-winter.

chapters.title: Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the house's final gathering before its sale, Cyrus returns uninvited and speaks the completed sentence to everyone assembled — not as accusation but as restoration, giving the vanished brother back his name. Some leave; Lise stays. Resolution: Cyrus loses the family's interior but gains their own — walking out into the cold having chosen justice outside any court, no longer needing the smile that ends conversations.
